fields.Name: sfmc
fields.Description: Salesforce Marketing Cloud Engagement (ExactTarget/Fuel) — dual REST+SOAP marketing platform: Data Extensions, Contacts, Journeys, Content Builder, Transactional Messaging, tracking events. OAuth2 client-credentials, tenant-subdomained hosts.

universalPK.note: No single vendor-wide PK field name exists — this vendor is split across two transports with different PK conventions. REST resources generally expose a bare 'id' field in their response envelope (confirmed on Campaigns: getCampaignCollection/getCampaign responseItemFields includes 'id'). SOAP APIObject-derived types carry a 3-tier fallback: ObjectID -> CustomerKey -> ID, in that preference order (per the vendor's own FuelSDK fallback logic, corroborated in sources/capabilities.json pkCandidate field for the 258 SOAP entries). This is a per-transport PK census summary for runtime SoftPKClassifier reference; each IO's own IsPrimaryKey selection is ioiof-extractor's job with its own evidence.

soap.evidence: sources/capabilities.json pkCandidate (258 SOAP entries); APIObject base type carries all three properties on every subtype

Transport.note: The vendor's own docs state: "The APIs don't have full parity, and you may need to use both SOAP and REST" (managing_enterprise_20_accounts_with_the_web_services_api.html family framing + vendor REST-first guidance: "existing SOAP API integrations only function with the Classic tools... all new Marketing Cloud technologies implement REST API"). A per-IO transport marker (x-sfmc-transport in the derived OpenAPI artifact) is MANDATORY on every IO row emitted by ioiof-extractor; this block is the integration-level explanation of that marker, not a substitute for it.

rest.note: 50 REST-side coverable leaf names (sources/transport-map.json), all new/modern surfaces per vendor guidance.

families: Generic Data Extension row CRUD (DataExtension/DataExtensionField/DataExtensionObject) — SOAP is the PRIMARY documented path; a REST rowset alternate exists per vendor knowledge but was NOT located as a titled page in the pinned 865-page Atlas snapshot (see DeclaredCapabilityLimits)
soapOnly.note: In practice SOAP-only per SOURCE_STUDY.md Step 5/Step 11: 258 SOAP-side coverable names total, only 5 (Asset/Campaign/Category/Message/Send) collide with a REST name of the same concept and are folded to REST-primary. The tracking-event family is reachable ONLY via the WSDL transitive closure (51 indirect-only APIObject descendants, all 10 tracking-event types among them) and has no REST equivalent anywhere in the pinned corpus.

crossTransportCollisions.evidence: vendor guidance: "existing SOAP API integrations only function with the Classic tools...all new Marketing Cloud technologies implement REST API"; recorded per-name in sources/transport-collisions.json
crossTransportCollisions.residualDoubt: Not independently verified that the SOAP-side and REST-side objects sharing an English name are the SAME underlying record vs. two distinct concepts that happen to share a word (SOURCE_STUDY.md Residual Doubt #10).

BaseURIModel.note: The v2/discovery and v2/userinfo responses (both confirmed in the pinned corpus: getBaseURLs.json returns links[].href for auth_instance_url/rest_instance_url; getUserInfo.json returns rest.rest_instance_url/rest.soap_instance_url) demonstrate the vendor returns tenant-specific instance URLs keyed off the access token/client context rather than a fixed host. The v2/token response itself is documented elsewhere (routes.json shows only its REQUEST params: grant_type/client_id/client_secret/scope/account_id — its response body schema was not captured as a distinct page in this pinned 865-page snapshot) but is well-established vendor behavior (rest_instance_url + soap_instance_url on the token response) corroborated by the two sibling auth endpoints that ARE fully documented here. The connector PREFERS whichever of these responses it has (token response first, falling back to discovery/userinfo) and falls back to substituting the connection subdomain into the template only if neither is available. NO host is ever baked. A bogus subdomain does not even resolve (NXDOMAIN), which is why there is no credential-free tenant host to probe.

Auth.tokenLifetimeEvidence: ImpliedFromExample — vendor best-practice guidance states "Don't request more than one access token every 20 minutes" and directs callers to use the expires_in response parameter to time refreshes (rate-limiting-best-practices.json); no literal expires_in VALUE was observed in a captured response example in this pinned corpus, so 1200s is the guideline-implied figure, not an eyeballed response value.
Auth.refreshPolicy: proactive — refresh before expiry, never rely on a 401 to discover expiry
Auth.note: Only client_credentials is in scope for this connector (server-to-server integration); authorization_code is documented for web/public app integrations and is out of scope for a backend connector.

rest.note: Param names MUST come from the vendor EXAMPLES, not the documentation TABLE: getCampaignCollection's JSON-Parameters table documents page/pageSize/orderBy (no $), while its own Example Request sends GET /hub/v1/campaigns?$page=1&$pageSize=2&$orderBy=Name ASC — a confirmed table-vs-example disagreement (tableVsExampleDisagreement=true in sources/rest-parsed.json), independently reproduced by INDEPENDENT_REVIEW.md's own live fetch of the same page, and corroborated a third time by the Postman collection's saved example URLs also using $page/$pageSize. Max page size is PER-ENDPOINT (campaigns: max=default=50 per its table description regex), never a global constant.

Incremental.soapDateFilter: SimpleFilterPart over a filterable date property (ModifiedDate; EventDate for tracking events) with greaterThan/between SimpleOperators
Incremental.soapSinceLastBatch: RetrieveAllSinceLastBatch — a server-side since-last-batch boolean flag on RetrieveRequest, documented separately from date-filtering (retrieving_all_records_since_last_batch.json, confirmed literal SOAP envelope example with <RetrieveAllSinceLastBatch>true</RetrieveAllSinceLastBatch>)
Incremental.rest: per-endpoint $filter / modified-date orderBy (e.g. campaigns' orderBy accepts ModifiedDate DESC as its documented default)
Incremental.note: TWO distinct SOAP mechanisms exist (date-filter vs. since-last-batch) and are NOT interchangeable; record per-IO which one is PROVEN for that object, leaving both null where neither is. Vendor-level incremental capability is NOT uniform: sources/capabilities.json's script-derived per-object census (a modifiedDate/updatedDate/lastModified/eventDate/sendDate-shaped field observed in the example response or flattened WSDL element list) found incremental=proven for only 146/258 SOAP objects and 6/62 REST objects (pre-action-filter count) — most objects do NOT have a provable incremental field from the pinned corpus alone; treat incremental sync as a per-object capability, never a vendor-wide default.
Incremental.timezoneSemantics: SOAP APIObject ModifiedDate/CreatedDate are xsd:dateTime; REST modifiedDate/createdDate fields observed as ISO 8601 in example responses. No explicit vendor statement of a canonical account timezone for watermark comparison was located in the pinned corpus — v2/userinfo DOES return an organization-level zoneinfo/timezone block (getUserInfo.json), which is the credential-free-inaccessible source of truth for account timezone; a connector MUST NOT assume UTC without reading this field for the connected account, since a wrong-timezone assumption silently skips or re-reads rows at a watermark boundary.

DynamicObjectModel.discoveredAtRuntime: the individual Data Extensions of THIS connection and their columns

rowRead.primaryEvidence: managing_data_in_data_extensions.json — literal SOAP Create/Retrieve PHP sample against DataExtensionObject with CustomerKey
rowRead.alternateEvidence: NOT located as a distinct titled page in the pinned 865-page Atlas snapshot (grep for 'customobjectdata' across the full snapshot returns 0 hits). This is a well-known, real SFMC REST endpoint from general vendor-API knowledge, but its doc page was either not in-scope of the fetched mc-apis TOC subtree or did not title-parse to a METHOD /path form captured by parse-rest-pages.mjs. Recorded here as a DECLARED alternate per the architecture's own DynamicObjectModel convention, but flagged UNVERIFIED-FROM-PINNED-SOURCES — see DeclaredCapabilityLimits and METADATA_REPORT negative space.

DynamicObjectModel.contactAttributes: Contact attribute sets/schemas are likewise tenant-defined (attributeSetsData*/retrieveAttributeGroups* REST pages describe the mechanism, not any tenant's actual attribute schema)
DynamicObjectModel.rule: The MECHANISM is Declared (vendor-wide, every tenant has it); the DATA EXTENSIONS are Discovered per connection. Baking any tenant DE list or DE column into Declared metadata is the tenant-specific-metadata defect this architecture forbids; declaring no DE mechanism at all is the opposite defect — a connector that cannot read the vendor central data structure.

soap.shape: SOAP Fault with a custom <apifault> detail block carrying Code + Message
soap.throttleEvidence: rate-limiting.json — literal sample HTTP 500 SOAP fault payload: faultstring>Rate Limited</faultstring>, apifault Code=17 Message="Rate Limited"
soap.classifyErrorGuidance: Treat SOAP HTTP 500 as potentially-throttle-and-retryable (inspect the fault detail for Code=17/"Rate Limited" before deciding fatal-vs-retryable), NOT as an unconditional fatal error — this vendor documents 500 as ITS throttle signal for SOAP specifically.

rest.shape: JSON body { message, errorcode, documentation } on validation/business errors (error-handling.json numeric custom-code table: 10000-10006 validation, 20000-20002 authorization, 30000-30006 runtime); throttle-specific body adds retryAfter
rest.throttleEvidence: rate-limiting-errors.json — literal sample: HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests, Retry-After: 5, body {"message":"Rate limit exceeded","errorcode":50100,"retryAfter":5,...} and a second variant errorcode 50200 with no Retry-After ("Your requests are temporarily blocked.")
rest.classifyErrorGuidance: Honor 429 + Retry-After when present (errorcode 50100); when Retry-After is absent (errorcode 50200, temporary block) fall back to exponential backoff per the vendor's own best-practices page. A generic REST 500 ("Internal Server Error", per error-handling.json's own table) is NOT documented as this vendor's REST throttle signal — REST throttling is 429, SOAP throttling is 500. Do not conflate the two transports' throttle-status conventions.

ErrorModel.note: CORRECTION to a plan-time assumption: throttling does NOT surface as HTTP 500 vendor-wide. It surfaces as HTTP 500 (with a SOAP-fault payload) on the SOAP transport specifically (rate-limiting.json), and as HTTP 429 (with a structured JSON body, sometimes with Retry-After) on the REST transport specifically (rate-limiting-errors.json) — these are two DIFFERENT, transport-specific vendor pages with two different documented statuses. ClassifyError must branch on transport, not apply a single 500-means-throttle rule everywhere.

Configuration.DiscoveryIsAuthoritativeNote: There is NO describe-ALL-objects endpoint. SOAP Describe answers per-object; Retrieve DataExtension enumerates that business unit's DEs (authoritative for the DE tier ONLY — a tenant's actual DE list IS fully enumerable via this call, unlike every other object family); /platform/v1/endpoints and the Journey REST discovery document cover their own slices. Mixed coverage means absence proves nothing for every family EXCEPT the DE tier itself, so NOTHING may ever be deactivated from a discovery result except possibly a DE confirmed absent from a live Retrieve DataExtension enumeration for that specific business unit. Record this DE-tier nuance explicitly so a future build can reason about it without re-deriving.

OutOfScopeObjectFamilies.reason: A DIFFERENT product built natively on Salesforce Core with Data 360 (Data Cloud) unified profiles and Flow Builder, addressed through Salesforce CORE APIs on *.salesforce.com with core OAuth — not ExactTarget infrastructure, not Data Extensions, not Journey Builder, not *.marketingcloudapis.com. It shares a brand family with this product and nothing else. Any MCN route, host, auth shape or unified-profile object appearing in this emission is a defect, not an extension.

A different B2B marketing-automation product with its own API (pi.pardot.com / Salesforce core API, Pardot Business Unit scoping). Not reachable through the Engagement token and not part of this catalog.
A different analytics product with its own API surface and auth; no object overlap with the Engagement catalog.

OutOfScopeObjectFamilies.family: Marketing Cloud Personalization (fka Interaction Studio / Evergage)
OutOfScopeObjectFamilies.reason: A different personalization product on its own hosts with its own auth; no object overlap with the Engagement catalog.

OutOfScopeObjectFamilies.family: Salesforce CRM (Sales/Service Cloud) sObject + SOQL surface
OutOfScopeObjectFamilies.reason: A different system that ALREADY has its own connector at connectors-registry/salesforce. SFMC Engagement is not a Salesforce-CRM derivative and must not COMPOSE on it: no SOQL, no /services/data, no sObject describe conventions.
Separate (and in Social Studio's case retired) products with separate surfaces; not part of the Engagement REST/SOAP catalog.

OutOfScopeObjectFamilies.family: Marketing Cloud for AppExchange (MC Connect) configuration API
OutOfScopeObjectFamilies.reason: The Atlas docs carry a 50-node "Marketing Cloud for Appexchange API Guide" subtree describing how a Salesforce CRM org is WIRED to Engagement (connector configuration, sync setup). It documents a deployment boundary, not Engagement record types. Recorded as a known sibling so the universe count stays honest.

OutOfScopeObjectFamilies.family: Message-send and journey-fire ACTION operations (Transactional Messaging sends, Fire Entry Event, Push/SMS send-to-list/contact, Refresh List)
OutOfScopeObjectFamilies.reason: These are ACTION-shaped operations (send a message, fire an event, refresh an audience) and BULK/ASYNC jobs, not per-record create/update of a durable record. They are ENUMERATED and recorded in Configuration as per-object out-of-scope ACTIONS with their shapes (candidates for a future MJ Action), never silently dropped and never mis-wired into CreateRecord — which would make a green CRUD test meaningless. Their DEFINITION records (send definitions, message definitions, journeys, push/SMS message definitions) ARE in scope as records.

OutOfScopeObjectFamilies.family: Event Notification Service webhook DELIVERY transport
OutOfScopeObjectFamilies.reason: ENS pushes events to a customer-hosted callback; the receiving side is not a pull surface this connector can sync. The ENS CONFIGURATION records (callbacks, subscriptions) ARE in scope as CRUD records — only the inbound webhook transport is excluded.

OutOfScopeObjectFamilies.family: Enhanced SFTP / Automation Studio file-drop transport
OutOfScopeObjectFamilies.reason: Engagement also exchanges data by SFTP file drop driven by Automation Studio. That is a file transport, not an API object family; the Automation/Activity DEFINITION objects that schedule it ARE in scope. Recorded as awareness for a future file-feed capability.

OutOfScopeObjectFamilies.family: AMPscript / SSJS / Guide Template Language content surfaces
OutOfScopeObjectFamilies.reason: Server-side content languages rendered inside emails and CloudPages. They carry no durable syncable records; the ASSETS that contain them are in scope via Content Builder.

OutOfScopeObjectFamilies.family: Narrative / conceptual documentation (SOAP Technical Articles, SOAP Simple Development Scenarios, REST conceptual/guide pages, API Best Practices & API Errors top-level branches)
OutOfScopeObjectFamilies.reason: 233 total TOC leaves (148 SOAP Technical Articles + 10 SOAP Simple Development Scenarios + 77 REST conceptual/guide pages that did not title-parse to METHOD /path + the API Best Practices/API Errors top-level branches) are prose walkthroughs, per-language code-sample galleries, and vendor-wide best-practice/error references — not object or endpoint documentation. None describe a syncable record type. Added to this list (missing from the plan-time draft) upon reconciliation against SOURCE_STUDY.md's INFORMATIONAL taxonomies F/G/I/J so their exclusion is accounted-for, not silently dropped.

OutOfScopeObjectFamilies.family: SOAP operation-envelope & query-primitive wrapper types (Create/Retrieve/Update/Delete/Perform/Schedule/Configure/Extract/Execute x Options/Result/Request/Response, plus SimpleFilterPart/ComplexFilterPart/TagFilterPart/LogicalOperators/SimpleOperators/Query/QueryObject/QueryRequest)
OutOfScopeObjectFamilies.reason: 37 SOAP schemas structurally resemble record types (they carry a Name/DataType properties table) but are SOAP-method-call plumbing — parameters and results of an operation, not independently listable/retrievable business objects with their own identity. Reclassified out of the record-type bucket by scripts/reclassify-operation-envelopes.mjs (name-pattern match, script-derived not hand-picked). Added upon reconciliation against SOURCE_STUDY.md INFORMATIONAL taxonomy B.

62 xsd:simpleType restriction/enumeration definitions in the WSDL are vocabulary (valid values for a property on a real object), not record types themselves. Added upon reconciliation against SOURCE_STUDY.md INFORMATIONAL taxonomy C.

Configuration.OutOfScopeObjectFamiliesNote: No Engagement object family and no documented Engagement record operation is out of scope beyond what is listed above — this build models the FULL documented Engagement REST+SOAP surface (266 TaxonomyLeaves per SOURCE_STUDY.md Step 10). The three entries appended during this pass (narrative documentation, SOAP operation-envelopes, SOAP simple-type enums) were found in SOURCE_STUDY.md's INFORMATIONAL taxonomy table but were missing from the plan-time draft of this list; added here as directed by the reconciliation instruction, each with its own SOURCE_STUDY.md citation.

ActionCatalogSummary.note: Full per-entry shapes (endpoint, parent-object binding, verb) live in the pinned action-catalog.json rather than being duplicated inline here — every entry there is a candidate for a future MJ Action, never silently dropped. 5 REST action-shaped ops are bound to a parent resource (e.g. assetAdvancedQuery POST .../assets/query bound to Asset); 84 are SOAP Perform/Schedule/Configure-verb CRUD-matrix rows (state-transition/provisioning calls, e.g. soapPerformCampaign, soapScheduleAutomation — never a genuine field-level CRUD write); 2 are the async data-extension-rowset submit-then-poll bulk jobs (insertDataExtensionIDAsync/updateDataExtensionIDAsync).

DeclaredCapabilityLimits.reason: No free Marketing Cloud Engagement developer sandbox exists (an Installed Package + a real, paid tenant is required to obtain client_id/client_secret at all — confirmed structurally by authenticate-soap-api.json's own onboarding instructions: "Obtain a client ID and secret by creating a package in Marketing Cloud with an API Integration component", which presupposes an existing paid Marketing Cloud account; no self-serve trial-signup page was located in the pinned corpus).
DeclaredCapabilityLimits.consequence: The credential-free ceiling is the honest ceiling for this connector build. Lifting it requires a real tenant Installed Package plus an sfmc-readonly broker plan. RECORDED so this is never rediscovered.

DeclaredCapabilityLimits.reason: No tenant host resolves without a credential — a bogus subdomain does not even resolve (NXDOMAIN) against *.auth/*.rest/*.soap.marketingcloudapis.com.
DeclaredCapabilityLimits.consequence: Credential-free probing is limited to the legacy tenant-agnostic gateway at www.exacttargetapis.com, and ONLY at SERVICE-PREFIX granularity (confirmed live during Stage-2 independent review: real service prefixes [hub/v1, asset/v1, contacts/v1, interaction/v1, automation/v1, data/v1, messaging/v1, platform/v1] returned HTTP 401 Not Authenticated; a bogus prefix/version returned HTTP 596 Service Not Found per error-handling.json's own table; a bogus LEAF under a real prefix [/hub/v1/notarealthing] ALSO returned 401 — i.e. the gateway confirms a service exists but cannot confirm any specific leaf path exists credential-free). See INDEPENDENT_REVIEW.md 'Gateway probe discrimination' row.

DeclaredCapabilityLimits.reason: No describe-ALL-objects endpoint exists; SOAP Describe/REST discovery each cover their own slice (see DiscoveryIsAuthoritativeNote).
DeclaredCapabilityLimits.consequence: Never deactivate an IO or a discovered record on absence from any single discovery call, except a Data Extension itself, which the SOAP Retrieve DataExtension call CAN authoritatively enumerate for one business unit.

DeclaredCapabilityLimits.reason: The vendor's own guidance states existing SOAP integrations and new REST surfaces are not full substitutes for one another ("existing SOAP API integrations only function with the Classic tools").
DeclaredCapabilityLimits.consequence: Some families are SOAP-only (all 10 tracking-event types, Classic content, generic DE row CRUD's PRIMARY path) and a REST-only connector would silently omit them. Both transports must be implemented.

DeclaredCapabilityLimits.reason: rate-limiting.json / rate-limiting-errors.json / rate-limiting-best-practices.json all describe throttling as reactive and account-specific ("Marketing Cloud reserves the right to throttle... depends on the rate necessary to stabilize operations") with NO published numeric requests-per-second/minute ceiling anywhere in the pinned corpus.
DeclaredCapabilityLimits.consequence: BatchMaxRequestCount/BatchRequestWaitTime are left NULL on this Integration row rather than fabricated. Inventing a number would be a fabricated capability claim.

DeclaredCapabilityLimits.reason: SOAP throttling surfaces as HTTP 500 with a SOAP fault payload (rate-limiting.json); REST throttling surfaces as HTTP 429 with a structured JSON body and often Retry-After (rate-limiting-errors.json). These are two DIFFERENT vendor pages with two DIFFERENT documented statuses — see ErrorModel.note for the explicit correction of a plan-time assumption that this was a single vendor-wide 500 rule.
DeclaredCapabilityLimits.consequence: ClassifyError must apply adaptive backoff on SOAP 500 (inspecting the fault detail before deciding fatal-vs-retryable) AND on REST 429/Retry-After, as two distinct branches, not one.

DeclaredCapabilityLimits.reason: Data Extension schemas (and Contact attribute sets) are entirely customer-defined at runtime; no public doc enumerates any tenant's actual DE columns.
DeclaredCapabilityLimits.consequence: Field/object absence for a specific tenant's Data Extension proves nothing about the vendor-wide mechanism; DE column discovery is a connector runtime concern, not a metadata-authoring concern.

DeclaredCapabilityLimits.reason: Vendor best-practice guidance ties token reuse to a ~20-minute cadence ("Don't request more than one access token every 20 minutes", rate-limiting-best-practices.json) and directs callers to the expires_in response parameter for the authoritative value.
DeclaredCapabilityLimits.consequence: Proactive refresh (using expires_in, refreshing ahead of expiry) is mandatory for any sync longer than ~20 minutes; never rely on a 401 to discover expiry.

DeclaredCapabilityLimits.reason: UNPROVEN. Planning-time external research surfaced a claim that non-sendable Data Extensions cap REST rowset retrieval at 200 rows while sendable ones do not; a targeted grep of the pinned Atlas corpus's postDataExtensionRowsetByKey/getResultsDataExtensionAsync pages for an explicit sendable-vs-non-sendable row-cap statement did NOT turn up a load-bearing sentence in this pass (SOURCE_STUDY.md Residual Doubt #6). Also relevant: the REST rowset endpoint path itself was not located as a titled page at all in this pinned snapshot (see DynamicObjectModel.rowRead.alternateEvidence).
DeclaredCapabilityLimits.consequence: Do NOT branch connector logic on sendable-vs-non-sendable DE filtering behavior until independently confirmed against a live account. Recorded as UNPROVEN, not as a fact.

DeclaredCapabilityLimits.reason: No official vendor-published OpenAPI/Swagger spec exists for the REST surface; sfmc-engagement-openapi.derived.json is SCRIPT-DERIVED from the Atlas prose docs + CRUD matrix, not vendor-authored.
DeclaredCapabilityLimits.consequence: T7 (spec-conformance verification) is LINT here — validated against the derived artifact's own internal consistency and against the live Atlas prose — not external verification against a vendor contract.

Configuration.APIVersioningStrategyNote: URL-path segment, but NOT globally uniform: all REST resource-family paths observed carry /v1/ immediately after the service prefix (hub/v1, asset/v1, contacts/v1, interaction/v1, automation/v1, data/v1, messaging/v1, platform/v1, sms/v1, push/v1 — 10 distinct service prefixes observed across sources/rest-parsed.json). The Auth service specifically uses /v2/ (v2/token, v2/userinfo, v2/discovery, routes.json) — a different version number under a different service. Do not assume a single vendor-wide version constant.
Configuration.CustomObjectMarkerPatternGap: No naming-convention marker for custom objects was located. Unlike e.g. HubSpot's p_<accountID>_<name>, SFMC's customer-custom-object mechanism (Data Extensions) has no distinguishing name prefix — a Data Extension IS the custom-object primitive itself, not a marked subset of a larger object catalog. Left NULL; see DynamicObjectModel for the actual mechanism.
Configuration.CustomFieldMarkerPatternGap: No naming-convention marker for custom fields was located in the pinned corpus. Left NULL.
Configuration.WebhooksEvidence: ens-notification-signing.json — explicit statement: "Marketing Cloud Event Notification Service signs every notification delivered to your callback with an HMAC-SHA256 signature... compare the HMAC-SHA256 signature to the value in x-sfmc-ens-signature." ENS callback/subscription CONFIGURATION is in-scope as CRUD records (createCallback/createSubscription/etc.); the inbound webhook DELIVERY transport itself is out of scope (see OutOfScopeObjectFamilies).
Configuration.BulkOperationsEvidence: sources/rest-parsed.json — insertDataExtensionIDAsync (POST /data/v1/async/dataextensions/{id}/rows) and updateDataExtensionIDAsync (PUT, same path) submit a job; getStatusDataExtensionAsync (GET /data/v1/async/{requestId}/status) and getResultsDataExtensionAsync (GET /data/v1/async/{requestId}/results) poll it — a genuine async submit-then-poll pattern, distinct from the SOAP-side Perform/Schedule/Configure action verbs (see ActionCatalogSummary).
Configuration.TokenRefreshStrategyNote: See Auth.refreshPolicy/Auth.tokenLifetimeSeconds for the full evidence — restated here at the top level because TokenRefreshStrategy is named as its own Configuration slot in the extraction directive.

WriteCapability.soap: Create/Update/Delete verbs exist per the CRUD matrix (sources/soap-crud-matrix.json, 85 unique object names with Create/Retrieve/Update/Delete/Perform/Schedule/Configure columns) — write support is genuinely PER-OBJECT, not uniform. Tracking events (SentEvent, OpenEvent, etc.) are Retrieve-only by their nature (they are system-generated log records); DataExtensionObject/DataExtension/Contact-adjacent objects (Subscriber, List) support Create/Update/Delete per the matrix.
WriteCapability.rest: Create/Update(PATCH or PUT)/Delete verbs observed per-resource in sources/rest-parsed.json (Methods: GET 75 / POST 76 / PATCH 5 / PUT 13 / DELETE 20) — again per-object, not uniform. Some REST families are read-only or action-only (see OutOfScopeObjectFamilies action-not-record-crud entry and ActionCatalogSummary).
WriteCapability.note: Per-IO WriteCapability (hasCreate/hasUpdate/hasDelete) is captured per-object in sources/capabilities.json by ioiof-extractor's own evidence; this vendor-level note establishes that write capability gates on the OBJECT, never assume vendor-wide uniform CRUD.

Configuration.ConcurrencyControlEvidence: A corpus-wide scan of all 865 pinned Atlas pages (excluding manifest.json) for the literal strings 'ETag' and 'If-Match' returned 0 hits on both (see CODE_EVIDENCE — extract-sfmc-facts.py concurrencyControlScan). No optimistic-concurrency header or version-token mechanism is documented anywhere in the pinned corpus for either transport. Journeys (Interactions) carry their own domain-specific versionNumber field (see deleteInteractionById.json), but that is a JOURNEY-VERSIONING feature (multiple named versions of one journey), not a generic optimistic-concurrency control usable for conflict detection on arbitrary writes.
Configuration.ConcurrencyControlConsequence: No real MostRecent conflict resolution is possible from vendor-native concurrency tokens; conflict handling, if bidirectional is ever enabled, must be snapshot-3-way only (compare last-synced snapshot vs. current source vs. current destination), never an ETag/If-Match-based optimistic check.

DeleteSemantics.default: varies-by-object — NOT vendor-uniform, see per-family notes below

contacts.evidence: DeleteByContactIDs.json (POST /contacts/v1/contacts/actions/delete?type=ids) — EXPLICIT vendor statement: the call is asynchronous and QUEUED ('each process can take several hours to complete'); phase 1 is a SUPPRESSION ('A successful call suppresses any sends or other activities to the specified contacts for a specified number of days... Users may still see the contact record'); phase 2 after the configurable suppression window is an IRREVERSIBLE hard delete ('Marketing Cloud deletes the contact from all lists and sendable data extensions. You cannot restore any contact information associated with this delete process'). The suppression window is tenant-configurable via a separate 'Configure Settings for Deleting Contacts' resource.
contacts.softDeleteFlagField: not a boolean flag — the tombstone state is implicit in the suppression window, not an inspectable field on the Contact record itself as far as this pinned corpus shows

dataExtensionRows.evidence: No explicit soft-delete/tombstone statement was located for SOAP DataExtensionObject Delete or the REST rowset delete path in this pass. Treat as immediate hard delete until independently confirmed; do NOT assume orphan-deletion is safe without a live-account check.

genericSoapObjects.evidence: The CRUD matrix documents WHICH objects support a Delete verb (85 rows) but not the tombstone-vs-hard-delete SEMANTICS of that verb per object; this is a per-IO extraction task, not resolvable vendor-wide from the pinned corpus.

DeleteSemantics.consequence: Orphan-deletion propagation must default OFF except where an object's DeleteSemantics is independently proven hard/soft with evidence. Contacts specifically require respecting the tenant's configured suppression window before treating a delete as final.

Configuration.DefaultSyncDirectionNote: Read-only Pull is the recommended default for EVERY object in this catalog per this build's read-first, bidirectional-opt-in discipline. This is independent of any per-object WriteCapability finding above — write CAPABILITY existing at the vendor does not make write DEFAULT-safe against a client's real Marketing Cloud tenant.
Configuration.DefaultConflictResolutionNote: IF bidirectional sync is later enabled for a specific object (opt-in, never default), the recommended conflict-resolution policy is Manual, NOT MostRecent — because ConcurrencyControl is 'none' (no ETag/If-Match/version token found anywhere in the pinned corpus, see ConcurrencyControlEvidence), so there is no vendor-native mechanism to reliably determine which side is actually 'most recent' at write time. DestWins/SourceWins are also not recommended as defaults because SFMC Contact deletes are irreversible after the suppression window (see DeleteSemantics.contacts) and SOAP writes on tracking-derived objects would corrupt system-of-record log data — a human must arbitrate. Preconditions before ANY bidirectional default could be safely reconsidered for a specific object: (1) that object's WriteCapability is independently proven (not just CRUD-matrix-declared) against a live account, (2) that object's DeleteSemantics is independently proven (hard vs. soft, and for Contacts specifically the exact suppression-window behavior) against a live account, (3) a sandbox validation pass exists (this vendor has NO free sandbox — see DeclaredCapabilityLimits no-free-sandbox — so this precondition is currently UNMET for every object in this catalog and bidirectional must stay opt-in-with-explicit-allowWrite for the foreseeable future).

SFMCObjectTypeCatalog.note: MetadataWriter gap-fill pass (2026-09-08). Maps SOAP/REST object-type identifiers (from the identity/ioiof-extractor residual gap list) to a classification (record-type = independently retrievable/creatable object; enum = simpleType/enumerated value set; helper = supporting non-object construct with no extractable Properties/Values table) and a reproducible evidence pointer. Sources restricted to the declared SOURCE_BUNDLE: etframework.partnerAPI.wsdl (SOAP WSDL, sdkPaths), sfmc-engagement-openapi.derived.json (openapiPath, incl. the x-sfmc-soap-objecttype extension), atlas-mc-apis-snapshot/*.json (vendorDocsPaths). fields.Name: messageType
fields.Description: Indicates the type of message to create using the following integer values: 1 - Outbound (default), 3 - Location Entry, 4 - Location Exit, 5 - Beacon, 8 - Inbox

fields.Name: contentType
fields.Description: Indicates the content included within the message using the following integer values: 1 - Alert (default), 2 - Inbox, 3 - Inbox+Alert

fields.Name: name
fields.Description: Name of the message. Must be 100 or fewer characters. For Content Builder messages, use this format: content name-unique identifier. For example: 'my test content message-0debaa7a11e11b0a00b12345ef384b1z'.

fields.Name: application
fields.Description: App used to send message

fields.Name: application.id
fields.Description: The ID of the application

fields.Name: application.name
fields.Description: The name of the application

fields.Name: alert
fields.Description: Message displayed on the mobile device

fields.Name: sound
fields.Description: Used to override the value on the push message definition. Indicates the sound file to play when the push message arrives on the mobile device. Name must include 100 or less characters.

fields.Name: badge
fields.Description: Available for both iOS and Android. For iOS SDK version 4.9.5 and newer: Overrides the value on the push message definition. Badge count displays this number in a badge on the app and increments this number by one for each new unread message. For older iOS SDK versions: Overrides the value on the push message definition. Badge count does not increment.

fields.Name: content-available
fields.Description: Integer value indicating the availability of content for an application enabled to use background push. Set this value to 1 to deliver the message as a silent push. This parameter applies only to apps integrated with the background push functionality available in iOS and Android. Note that you can use background push functionality in all apps with iOS 7 and Newsstand apps in iOS 6.

fields.Name: openDirect
fields.Description: Used to override the value on the push message definition. This value determines the location within the app that an app user views when they open that app via a push message. Assigned values must include 15 or less characters.

fields.Name: keys
fields.Description: Used to override the value on the push message definition. An array of Key/Value pairs that correspond to customer values defined in MobilePush.

fields.Name: custom
fields.Description: Specify the actual request body of the push message to precisely align that request body to your specifications.

fields.Name: sendInitiator
fields.Description: Indicates the method used to initiate the send for a push message using the following integer values: 0 - UI-based send, 1 - API (default), 2 - Automation, 3 - Journey Builder

fields.Name: startDate
fields.Description: Date and time when the message becomes available for sends. Uses a default value of the message creation time.

fields.Name: endDate
fields.Description: Date and time when the message is no longer available for sends. This optional parameter applies only to messages whose contentType is CloudPage or Alert+CloudPage. endDate must be after startDate.

fields.Name: messagesPerPeriod
fields.Description: Integer value indicating the number of messages that can send during a specified time period to throttle the volume of users responding to the notification. Use only when sendInitiator value equals 0.

fields.Name: minutesPerPeriod
fields.Description: Integer value indicating the number of minutes included in a specified time period. Use only when sendInitiator value equals 0.

fields.Name: numberOfPeriods
fields.Description: Indicates the time span of the period using the following integer values: 1 - Year, 2 - Month, 3 - Week, 4 - Day, 5 - Hour

fields.Name: isRollingPeriod
fields.Description: Boolean value indicating whether the limit resets after a rolling time period window or ends at a specified time

fields.Name: messageLimit
fields.Description: Integer values indicating the total number of times a messages displays on a mobile device

fields.Name: title
fields.Description: The title to be used in place of the message's original title.

fields.Name: subtitle
fields.Description: The subtitle to be used in place of the message's original subtitle. This setting applies only to push notification alerts.

fields.Name: mutable-content
fields.Description: If true, rich push functionality is enabled for the message.

fields.Name: tzBased
fields.Description: Boolean value indicating whether a send occurs based on the specified time zone for a mobile device, as reflected in the contact record. To ensure timely delivery for each timezone, make sure that any dependent data extensions and audiences are available to be refreshed up to 14 hours prior to the scheduled send time. Uses a default value of false. Use only when sendInitiator value equals 0.

fields.Name: tzPastSendAction
fields.Description: Indicates the action to perform when a time-zone-based send occurs and that send time already passed for some time zones. Uses the following string values: 1 - Send immediately (default), 2 - Send at scheduled time, next day, 3 - Never send

fields.Name: scheduleTzOffset
fields.Description: Integer value indicating the time zone offset. Uses a default value of -6.

fields.Name: scheduledTzSupportsDst
fields.Description: Boolean value indicating whether the scheduled time zone supports Daylight Savings Time. Uses a default value of false.

fields.Name: inclusionLists

fields.Name: exclusionLists
fields.Description: Array of list ID values indicating the lists excluded from receiving the send. Use only when sendInitiator value equals 0.

fields.Name: status
fields.Description: Indicates the status of the message using the following integer values:: 1 - Draft, 2 - Active (default), 3 - Inactive, 4 - Deleted

fields.Name: pageId
fields.Description: Integer values indicating the page associated with the message for CloudPage and Alert+CloudPage sends

fields.Name: url
fields.Description: String value indicating the URL for the page associated with the message for CloudPage and Alert+CloudPage sends

fields.Name: subject

fields.Name: media

Configuration.unlistableReason: PARENT-SCOPED AND UN-ENUMERABLE: the collection GET /messaging/v1/messageDefinitionSends/key:{key}/deliveryRecords is real, but reaching it requires a messageDefinitionSends key that this API provides no way to enumerate. The parent family /messaging/v1/messageDefinitionSends publishes exactly ONE operation in the pinned source -- POST /messaging/v1/messageDefinitionSends/{triggeredSendDefinitionId}/send, actionShaped=true -- with no list and no get-by-id, and the delivery-records operation's own parameter table additionally marks RecipientSendId Required, a GUID that exists only as the return value of that send. So the records are reachable only by the caller who just performed a send, never by enumeration from a cold start. Declared here rather than silently dropped, and deliberately NOT given a Configuration.pathParams value: any key baked into shipped metadata would be one tenant's, and a wrong one would issue invalid requests against every other tenant. Evidence: packages/Integration/connectors-registry/sfmc/sources/rest-resources.json, families "/messaging/v1/messageDefinitionSends" and "/messaging/v1/messageDefinitionSends/key::id/deliveryRecords".

fields.Name: messageType
fields.Description: Indicates the type of message to create using the following integer values: 1 - Outbound (default), 3 - Location Entry, 4 - Location Exit, 5 - Beacon, 8 - Inbox

fields.Name: contentType
fields.Description: Indicates the content included within the message using the following integer values: 1 - Alert (default), 2 - Inbox, 3 - Inbox+Alert

fields.Name: name
fields.Description: Name of the message. Must be 100 or fewer characters. For Content Builder messages, use this format: content name-unique identifier. For example: 'my test content message-0debaa7a11e11b0a00b12345ef384b1z'.

fields.Name: application
fields.Description: App used to send message

fields.Name: application.id
fields.Description: The ID of the application

fields.Name: application.name
fields.Description: The name of the application

fields.Name: alert
fields.Description: Message displayed on the mobile device

fields.Name: sound
fields.Description: Used to override the value on the push message definition. Indicates the sound file to play when the push message arrives on the mobile device. Name must include 100 or less characters.

fields.Name: badge
fields.Description: Available for both iOS and Android. For iOS SDK version 4.9.5 and newer: Overrides the value on the push message definition. Badge count displays this number in a badge on the app and increments this number by one for each new unread message. For older iOS SDK versions: Overrides the value on the push message definition. Badge count does not increment.

fields.Name: content-available
fields.Description: Integer value indicating the availability of content for an application enabled to use background push. Set this value to 1 to deliver the message as a silent push. This parameter applies only to apps integrated with the background push functionality available in iOS and Android. Note that you can use background push functionality in all apps with iOS 7 and Newsstand apps in iOS 6.

fields.Name: openDirect
fields.Description: Used to override the value on the push message definition. This value determines the location within the app that an app user views when they open that app via a push message. Assigned values must include 15 or less characters.

fields.Name: keys
fields.Description: Used to override the value on the push message definition. An array of Key/Value pairs that correspond to customer values defined in MobilePush.

fields.Name: custom
fields.Description: Specify the actual request body of the push message to precisely align that request body to your specifications.

fields.Name: sendInitiator
fields.Description: Indicates the method used to initiate the send for a push message using the following integer values: 0 - UI-based send, 1 - API (default), 2 - Automation, 3 - Journey Builder

fields.Name: startDate
fields.Description: Date and time when the message becomes available for sends. Uses a default value of the message creation time.

fields.Name: endDate
fields.Description: Date and time when the message is no longer available for sends. This optional parameter applies only to messages whose contentType is CloudPage or Alert+CloudPage. endDate must be after startDate.

fields.Name: messagesPerPeriod
fields.Description: Integer value indicating the number of messages that can send during a specified time period to throttle the volume of users responding to the notification. Use only when sendInitiator value equals 0.

fields.Name: minutesPerPeriod
fields.Description: Integer value indicating the number of minutes included in a specified time period. Use only when sendInitiator value equals 0.

fields.Name: numberOfPeriods
fields.Description: Indicates the time span of the period using the following integer values: 1 - Year, 2 - Month, 3 - Week, 4 - Day, 5 - Hour

fields.Name: isRollingPeriod
fields.Description: Boolean value indicating whether the limit resets after a rolling time period window or ends at a specified time

fields.Name: messageLimit
fields.Description: Integer values indicating the total number of times a messages displays on a mobile device

fields.Name: title
fields.Description: The title to be used in place of the message's original title.

fields.Name: subtitle
fields.Description: The subtitle to be used in place of the message's original subtitle. This setting applies only to push notification alerts.

fields.Name: mutable-content
fields.Description: If true, rich push functionality is enabled for the message.

fields.Name: tzBased
fields.Description: Boolean value indicating whether a send occurs based on the specified time zone for a mobile device, as reflected in the contact record. To ensure timely delivery for each timezone, make sure that any dependent data extensions and audiences are available to be refreshed up to 14 hours prior to the scheduled send time. Uses a default value of false. Use only when sendInitiator value equals 0.

fields.Name: tzPastSendAction
fields.Description: Indicates the action to perform when a time-zone-based send occurs and that send time already passed for some time zones. Uses the following string values: 1 - Send immediately (default), 2 - Send at scheduled time, next day, 3 - Never send

fields.Name: scheduleTzOffset
fields.Description: Integer value indicating the time zone offset. Uses a default value of -6.

fields.Name: scheduledTzSupportsDst
fields.Description: Boolean value indicating whether the scheduled time zone supports Daylight Savings Time. Uses a default value of false.

fields.Name: inclusionLists
fields.Description: Array of list ID values indicating the lists that will receive the send. Use only when sendInitiator value equals 0.

fields.Name: exclusionLists
fields.Description: Array of list ID values indicating the lists excluded from receiving the send. Use only when sendInitiator value equals 0.

fields.Name: status
fields.Description: Indicates the status of the message using the following integer values:: 1 - Draft, 2 - Active (default), 3 - Inactive, 4 - Deleted

fields.Name: pageId
fields.Description: Integer values indicating the page associated with the message for CloudPage and Alert+CloudPage sends

fields.Name: url
fields.Description: String value indicating the URL for the page associated with the message for CloudPage and Alert+CloudPage sends

fields.Name: subject
fields.Description: String value indicating the subject line used for the message

fields.Name: media
fields.Description: Rich media to include in the message

fields.Name: media.androidUrl
fields.Description: URL for the media to send to Android devices

fields.Name: media.iosUrl
fields.Description: URL for the media to send to iOS devices

fields.Name: media.alt
fields.Description: Text to display if the message cannot include the specified rich media

fields.Name: geofences
fields.Description: Array of string values indicating the geofences associated with the message send. Use only when sendInitiator value equals 1.

fields.Name: subscriptions.resubscribe
fields.Description: Forces the message send request to subscribe the mobile number back into a short code if a user may have requested STOP. Often used to ensure that critical transactional messages are delivered irrespective of a mobile number subscriber status.

fields.Name: content.message
fields.Description: Override for message content in the definition that you want sent with each message. Use substitution strings to personalize the content.

fields.Name: FooterContentArea

fields.Name: SuppressTracking
fields.Description: Indicates whether the send definition suppresses tracking results for associated sends.

fields.Name: IsSendLogging
fields.Description: Indicates whether send logging is enabled for the specified send definition

fields.Name: SendDefinitionList

fields.Name: Email

fields.Name: BccEmail
fields.Description: Indicates email addresses to receive blind carbon copy of a message. The BccEmail property allows access to the BCC feature if enabled on the account. It does not error out if feature is not enabled. The API returns no tracking information for BCC emails. You must specify this property in an email send definition, as you cannot specify this property at send time. You can create a profile attribute for this property and pass in a value at send time, however.

fields.Name: AutoBccEmail
fields.Description: Defines blind carbon copy email address to which to send a message as part of an email send definition.

fields.Name: TestEmailAddr
fields.Description: Defines an email address to which to send a test message as part of an email send definition.Use the Test action when sending a test email to an email send definition.

fields.Name: EmailSubject
fields.Description: Subject for an email send. This property is required when updating a user-initiated send definition. If you don't pass the new subject to the email send definition, it retains the old subject for that definition. You must also specify the send classification to use as part of the send.

fields.Name: DynamicEmailSubject
fields.Description: Contains content to be used in a dynamic subject line.

fields.Name: IsMultipart
fields.Description: Indicates whether the email is sent with Multipart/MIME enabled.

fields.Name: IsWrapped
fields.Description: Indicates whether an email send contains the links necessary to process tracking information for clicks.

fields.Name: SendLimit
fields.Description: Indicates limit of messages to send as part of a send definition within a predefined send window.

fields.Name: SendWindowOpen
fields.Description: Defines the beginning of a send window for a send definition.

fields.Name: SendWindowClose
fields.Description: Defines the end of a send window for a send definition.

fields.Name: SendWindowDelete
fields.Description: Indicates whether an existing send window for a send definition is deleted.

fields.Name: DeduplicateByEmail
fields.Description: Indicates whether a send definition de-duplicates multiple emails sent to the same email address. Set to true to ensure that only one message is sent to a single email address, if that email appears on several different lists or data extensions in a send definition.

fields.Name: ExclusionFilter
fields.Description: Contains a string of AMPscript that can evaluate to true or false, used to exclude email addresses from a send definition. If you include an ExclusionFilter in a create call, you must also include the SendDefinitionList property. The ExclusionFilter property can cause performance issues with send time for large amounts of email addresses. Use the data filter function if you experience performance problems.

fields.Name: TrackingUsers
fields.Description: Defines account users with access to tracking information for that send definition.

fields.Name: Additional
fields.Description: The ID for a send that customers use as a campaign ID. This property contains external campaign ID information or more metadata that appears in the tracking extract, and there is a personalization string for it. You can set this information at the time of the send or within an email send definition.

fields.Name: CCEmail
fields.Description: Carbon copy email address. You must specify the CCEmail property in an email send definition, as you cannot specify this property at send time. You can create a profile attribute for this property and pass in a value at send time, however.

fields.Name: DeliveryScheduledTime
fields.Description: Defines scheduled data and time for a send related to an email send definition.

fields.Name: MessageDeliveryType
fields.Description: Enumerates the types of message delivery options available for email send definitions. Valid values include: Standard - use as default unless your account is configured to handle burst sending DelayedDeliveryByMTAQueue

fields.Name: IsSeedListSend
fields.Description: Indicates whether a email send includes the use of a seed list.

fields.Name: TimeZone
fields.Description: Contains time zone information for an Account. For Create and Update calls, this property defines the time zone for an Account object. On a Retrieve call, TimeZone indicates which time zone is in effect for the Account object in question. Without a specific time zone, the Account defaults to Central Standard Time.

fields.Name: SeedListOccurance

fields.Name: ReplyToAddress
fields.Description: Specifies the reply address used for any messages sent using this send definition.

fields.Name: ReplyToDisplayName

accessPath.evidence: packages/Integration/connectors-registry/sfmc/sources/rest-resources.json family "/contacts/v1/contacts/id::id/Preferences" — operations POST /contacts/v1/contacts/id:{contactId}/Preferences ; GET /contacts/v1/contacts/id:{contactId}/Preferences

Configuration.unpageableEvidence: packages/Integration/connectors-registry/sfmc/sources/rest-resources.json family "/contacts/v1/contacts/id::id/Preferences" — POST /contacts/v1/contacts/id:{contactId}/Preferences ; GET /contacts/v1/contacts/id:{contactId}/Preferences — GET-collection exists; no page/pageSize/offset/limit parameter appears in any operation's parameter table or example URL (Atlas pageId addContactPreferencesById, getContactPreferencesById).
Configuration.primaryKeyReason: contactId is the record identity, and it is PATH-ADDRESSABLE rather than inferred: the vendor addresses this resource as /contacts/v1/contacts/id:{contactId}/Preferences, which returns exactly one preferences record per contact. Same basis on which ApplicationKey.key was retained during the PK-provenance rebuild (a value the documented URL form uses to address a single record is identifying). This object was briefly modelled as keyless because its payload also carries a write-result envelope (requestServiceMessageID, rowsInserted/rowsUpdated/rowsDeleted/rowsAffected, responseDateTime) and those fields are correctly NOT identity — requestServiceMessageID is a per-call correlation id that would grow duplicates every sync. Rejecting them was right; missing contactId was not. The object declares SupportsCreate (POST to the same path), and a writable object with no primary key CANNOT SAVE on PostgreSQL — MJ's save audit-wrapper emits an empty record identifier — so keyless + writable was an incoherent pair that the repo's lint:writable-pk gate correctly refused.

fields.Name: name
fields.Description: Name of the message. Must be 100 or fewer characters. For Content Builder messages, use this format: content name-unique identifier. For example: 'my test content message-0debaa7a11e11b0a00b12345ef384b1z'.

fields.Name: sound
fields.Description: Used to override the value on the push message definition. Indicates the sound file to play when the push message arrives on the mobile device. Name must include 100 or less characters.

fields.Name: badge
fields.Description: Available for both iOS and Android. For iOS SDK version 4.9.5 and newer: Overrides the value on the push message definition. Badge count displays this number in a badge on the app and increments this number by one for each new unread message. For older iOS SDK versions: Overrides the value on the push message definition. Badge count does not increment.

fields.Name: content-available
fields.Description: Integer value indicating the availability of content for an application enabled to use background push. Set this value to 1 to deliver the message as a silent push. This parameter applies only to apps integrated with the background push functionality available in iOS and Android. Note that you can use background push functionality in all apps with iOS 7 and Newsstand apps in iOS 6.

fields.Name: openDirect
fields.Description: Used to override the value on the push message definition. This value determines the location within the app that an app user views when they open that app via a push message. Assigned values must include 15 or less characters.

fields.Name: keys
fields.Description: Used to override the value on the push message definition. An array of Key/Value pairs that correspond to customer values defined in MobilePush.

fields.Name: custom
fields.Description: Specify the actual request body of the push message to precisely align that request body to your specifications.

fields.Name: sendInitiator
fields.Description: Indicates the method used to initiate the send for a push message using the following integer values: 0 - UI-based send, 1 - API (default), 2 - Automation, 3 - Journey Builder

fields.Name: startDate
fields.Description: Date and time when the message becomes available for sends. Uses a default value of the message creation time.

fields.Name: endDate
fields.Description: Date and time when the message is no longer available for sends. This optional parameter applies only to messages whose contentType is CloudPage or Alert+CloudPage. endDate must be after startDate.

fields.Name: messagesPerPeriod
fields.Description: Integer value indicating the number of messages that can send during a specified time period to throttle the volume of users responding to the notification. Use only when sendInitiator value equals 0.

fields.Name: minutesPerPeriod
fields.Description: Integer value indicating the number of minutes included in a specified time period. Use only when sendInitiator value equals 0.

fields.Name: numberOfPeriods
fields.Description: Indicates the time span of the period using the following integer values: 1 - Year, 2 - Month, 3 - Week, 4 - Day, 5 - Hour

fields.Name: isRollingPeriod
fields.Description: Boolean value indicating whether the limit resets after a rolling time period window or ends at a specified time

fields.Name: messageLimit
fields.Description: Integer values indicating the total number of times a messages displays on a mobile device

fields.Name: title
fields.Description: The title to be used in place of the message's original title.

fields.Name: subtitle
fields.Description: The subtitle to be used in place of the message's original subtitle. This setting applies only to push notification alerts.

fields.Name: mutable-content
fields.Description: If true, rich push functionality is enabled for the message.

fields.Name: tzBased
fields.Description: Boolean value indicating whether a send occurs based on the specified time zone for a mobile device, as reflected in the contact record. To ensure timely delivery for each timezone, make sure that any dependent data extensions and audiences are available to be refreshed up to 14 hours prior to the scheduled send time. Uses a default value of false. Use only when sendInitiator value equals 0.

fields.Name: tzPastSendAction
fields.Description: Indicates the action to perform when a time-zone-based send occurs and that send time already passed for some time zones. Uses the following string values: 1 - Send immediately (default), 2 - Send at scheduled time, next day, 3 - Never send

fields.Name: scheduleTzOffset
fields.Description: Integer value indicating the time zone offset. Uses a default value of -6.

fields.Name: scheduledTzSupportsDst
fields.Description: Boolean value indicating whether the scheduled time zone supports Daylight Savings Time. Uses a default value of false.

fields.Name: inclusionLists
fields.Description: Array of list ID values indicating the lists that will receive the send. Use only when sendInitiator value equals 0.

fields.Name: exclusionLists
fields.Description: Array of list ID values indicating the lists excluded from receiving the send. Use only when sendInitiator value equals 0.

fields.Name: status
fields.Description: Indicates the status of the message using the following integer values:: 1 - Draft, 2 - Active (default), 3 - Inactive, 4 - Deleted

fields.Name: pageId
fields.Description: Integer values indicating the page associated with the message for CloudPage and Alert+CloudPage sends

fields.Name: url
fields.Description: String value indicating the URL for the page associated with the message for CloudPage and Alert+CloudPage sends

fields.Name: subject
fields.Description: String value indicating the subject line used for the message

fields.Name: media

fields.Name: media.iosUrl
fields.Description: URL for the media to send to iOS devices

fields.Name: media.alt
fields.Description: Text to display if the message cannot include the specified rich media

fields.Name: geofences
